jobs.prompt:
fix(cpp): make the stored-value reader handle sparse arrays cheaply and preserve cyclic values

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
Branch `claude/cpp-gateway-port` contains `cpp/gateway/`: a finished module-for-module C++20 port of this repository's first-party TypeScript gateway (`src/`, `serve.ts`, `lib/jev_compaction/`): 325 application modules (`cpp/gateway/include/uos/**`, `cpp/gateway/src/**`), a JavaScript-semantics runtime layer `uos::rt` (`include/uos/rt`, `src/rt`, `src/runtime`) and 441 test binaries (`cpp/gateway/tests/**/*_test.cpp`, each a standalone program using the tiny harness `include/uos/rt/test.hpp`). The TypeScript is the behavioural ORACLE: expected values in tests were recorded from Bun 1.4.0, and the port reproduces Bun's observable behaviour. The optimised release build passes all 441 binaries / 5,023 cases on Linux ARM64 (GCC 16) and on macOS ARM64. Every deployment target is 64-bit ARM.

THE PROGRAMME YOU ARE PART OF
The owner's policy: generic functionality must come from mature open-source libraries, not hand-written code. `cpp/gateway/docs/OSS-REPLACEMENT-PLAN.md` ranks 55 runtime components with a verdict each; READ IT FIRST, then the row(s) for your component. JSON parsing (simdjson) and base64 (simdutf) are already done and are your worked examples: see `src/rt/json.cpp`, `src/rt/json_simdjson.hpp`, `src/rt/base64.cpp`, `third_party/simdjson`, `third_party/simdutf`, and how `CMakeLists.txt` registers third-party static libraries. About ten other agents are replacing OTHER components at the same time, each on its own clone; your branch will be merged with theirs, so stay strictly inside your OWNED paths and line ranges and keep unrelated code byte-identical (no reformatting, no renames, no drive-by fixes).

ALSO READ: `cpp/gateway/PORTING.md` (coroutine rules are mandatory: never bind structured bindings directly to a `co_await` result, never capture into a coroutine lambda that can outlive its frame), `cpp/gateway/docs/PORT-NOTES.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/TESTING.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/BUILD.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md`. PORTING.md's "Host safety" rules and "compile only through tools/unit.sh" apply to the authors' production server, NOT to your disposable runner: use compilers directly, in parallel. `tools/unit.sh`, `tools/env.sh` and the CMake presets contain host-specific absolute paths; do not depend on them. `python3 cpp/gateway/tools/links.py <test>` prints a test's application sources; every `src/rt/*.cpp` plus the vendored libraries that first-party code includes link into every test. `cpp/gateway/tools/ci_sanitize.py` is a small portable builder/runner (ASan+UBSan) you can copy the approach from: it resolves sources, compiles each once, links one binary per test.

YOUR MACHINE: a fresh GitHub-hosted Linux ARM64 runner (4 CPUs, 16 GB, sudo, network). Its distribution packages are too old for this tree (it needs Boost >= 1.86 with Boost.JSON, and a C++20 compiler newer than GCC 12 / Clang 18): install Clang 21 or newer from apt.llvm.org (or GCC 14+), and build Boost 1.92.0 `json` and `container` static libraries from the official source archive under a temp directory. Also needed: OpenSSL 3, SQLite >= 3.40, zlib, ICU, brotli, zstd development packages. Port flags: `-std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -Wshadow -Wconversion -Werror -DBOOST_JSON_NO_LIB -DBOOST_CONTAINER_NO_LIB -DBOOST_SYSTEM_NO_LIB -DBOOST_ASIO_DISABLE_AWAITABLE_FRAME_RECYCLING -DUOS_GATEWAY_NATIVE_LIBRARIES=1 -I cpp/gateway/include -I cpp/gateway`; third-party sources are compiled without the warning flags. Bun 1.4.0 is the oracle runtime: install exactly that version and, whenever you need to know what JavaScript does, RUN the TypeScript or a snippet under `bun --no-env-file`, do not guess.

RULES
- The library becomes the implementation. Keep only a thin shim for behaviour that JavaScript/Bun makes observable and the library does not provide (error messages and types, edge-case results, ordering). Where the plan says FAST-PATH, the existing code stays only as the declared exact-semantics fallback. If the library cannot reach parity without a shim about as large as the code it replaces, STOP, write that finding with evidence, and leave the component as it is: that is a valid result.
- Vendor each library UNMODIFIED under `cpp/gateway/third_party/<name>/` with its LICENSE, a `PROVENANCE.md` (upstream URL, tag, date, how obtained) and `SHA256SUMS`; download the exact release named in your task and verify the SHA-256 given there. Register it in `cpp/gateway/CMakeLists.txt` the way simdjson and simdutf are. Libraries already in the build (Boost 1.92, OpenSSL, ICU, zlib) are used as they are.
- ACCEPTANCE, all required: (1) every existing test and Bun-recorded differential vector that touches your component passes UNCHANGED (never edit an expected value; if you believe one is wrong, prove it under Bun and report it, do not change it); (2) add an equivalence test binary `cpp/gateway/tests/oss_<component>_equivalence_test.cpp` that feeds a broad fixed input set (include the existing test inputs, the Bun vectors, and at least a few thousand generated inputs from a seeded generator) through BOTH the old implementation and the new one and requires identical observable results; keep the old implementation available to that test (move it to `cpp/gateway/tests/legacy/` as a test-only source) so the comparison survives its deletion from production; (3) add an equivalence harness `cpp/gateway/fuzz/<component>_equivalence.cpp` in the style of the existing files in `cpp/gateway/fuzz/` that compares old and new on arbitrary bytes and calls `__builtin_trap()` on any difference, and register it in `cpp/gateway/fuzz/targets.json` with an `extra_sources` list (third-party and legacy sources it needs); the maintainer's CI runs it, you only build it and run it for two minutes as a smoke check; (4) measure old vs new on representative inputs (ns/op and, where relevant, allocations) and put the table in your report: the new path must not be slower; (5) then DELETE the replaced hand-written production code; (6) build with the port flags without warnings, and run the tests of your component plus every test whose link list includes your files, plain and under `-fsanitize=address,undefined`.
- Do not edit anything under `.github/`, the TypeScript, or `cpp/` outside `cpp/gateway/`. Do not touch `cpp/gateway/fuzz/ci.py`, `cpp/gateway/tools/ci_sanitize.py` or `docs/OSS-REPLACEMENT-PLAN.md` (the maintainer updates the plan from your report).
- The runner holds a model gateway token: never print it or write any credential to a file. Run tests with an empty `HOME`, a fresh `TMPDIR` and no provider variables.
- You can be cut off without warning. Commit after every meaningful step (the tree must build at each commit), write your report file EARLY and keep it current. Leave no build directories, binaries or downloads other than the vendored library in the checkout.

REPORT: `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/<job id>.md`: what was replaced and what was kept as a shim (with reasons), exact commands, real pass/fail counts, the before/after measurement table, lines of production code deleted and added, anything unfinished, and defects you found outside your owned paths (report, do not fix). End your final message with the same summary.

OWNED PATHS (you may create or edit only these)
- `cpp/gateway/src/rt/kv_jsc_deserialize.cpp`, `cpp/gateway/src/rt/kv_jsc.cpp`, `cpp/gateway/src/rt/kv_internal.hpp`, `cpp/gateway/src/rt/kv_value.cpp`, the KvValue parts of `cpp/gateway/include/uos/rt/kv.hpp` (about lines 163-531), the typed-value interchange and offline conversion sources that reject cycles (find them: `grep -rn "has no KvValue representation" cpp/gateway/src cpp/gateway/include`), and the tests of those components (additions only)
- your report, your equivalence test, your fuzz harness and its entry in `cpp/gateway/fuzz/targets.json`, `cpp/gateway/tests/legacy/<your component>*`, the `tests/LINKS.txt` lines for tests you add or whose link list your change alters, and the minimal `cpp/gateway/CMakeLists.txt` lines that register your library and sources.

TASK
Two known defects in the reader for values stored by Deno KV in JavaScriptCore's SerializedScriptValue format. This is not a library replacement (no library implements this format outside the JavaScript engines), so acceptance points (2)-(5) of the common rules are replaced by the ones here. DEFECT 1, memory amplification: a 13-byte stored value can declare an array of about 16.7 million elements (hex `05000000012cfbff00ffffffff`); the reader admits lengths up to `MaxMaterializedValues = 1<<24` and materialises every hole, costing hundreds of MiB, whereas JavaScript keeps such arrays sparse. Make memory and time proportional to the input size (represent hole runs / sparse arrays without materialising them) while returning exactly what Bun returns: run `Bun`'s `v8.deserialize`-equivalent path the TypeScript uses (see how `tests/rt/kv_jsc_deserialize_test.cpp` vectors were recorded and the Bun oracle helpers next to it) on this input and on at least ten more inputs you construct with large declared lengths, record the results as new vectors, and add a test asserting peak allocation stays under a few MiB for them. DEFECT 2, cycles: values containing object cycles or shared references are rejected with `TypeError: Typed-value interchange cycle has no KvValue representation` because the C++ value model is a tree (sites: `kv_jsc_deserialize.cpp` near line 545, `typed_value.cpp` near 512, `convert.cpp` near 227), while the TypeScript round-trips them; this blocks the offline database conversion tool. Give the model node identity (shared and cyclic references preserved through deserialise -> typed value -> convert -> serialise) and make the ORIGINAL unchanged cyclic proof fixture and tests pass, plus the existing acyclic ones. One design should solve both (a node graph with hole runs and back-references). Existing tests and Bun vectors must pass unchanged; add vectors, never edit them. Measure before/after on the existing benchmark inputs: no regression for ordinary values.
